statement: Let $\triangle ABC$ be acute, $A_1$ the foot of the altitude from $A$, $B_1$ and $C_1$ the projections of $A_1$ onto $AB$ and $AC$. Point $P$ makes convex quadrilateral $AB_1PC_1$ with the same area as $\triangle ABC$. Can $P$ lie strictly inside the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$?

Let $\alpha, \beta > 0$. Emerald starts at $(0,0)$, moves right or up each minute, staying in $|x-y| < 2025$. At each visited point $(x,y)$ she writes $\lfloor x\alpha + y\beta \rfloor$. If she writes each nonneg­ative integer exactly once, find all pairs $(\alpha, \beta)$.

Let $P(x)$ be a nonconstant integer polynomial with $P(0) \neq 0$. Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ be an infinite integer sequence with $P(i-j) \mid a_i - a_j$ for all distinct $i, j$. Prove the sequence is constant.

$n \geq 3$ cells on a circle, each assigned 0 or 1, with a rooster on one cell. If on 0: change to 1, move counterclockwise. If on 1: change to 0, move two counterclockwise. Prove that after sufficiently many operations, whenever the rooster is at cell $C$, it goes around exactly 3 times and returns to $C$ with all values the same as before those 3 rounds.
Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ be positive integers with $100!(a_m + \cdots + a_n) \mid a_{n-m+1}a_{m+n}$ for all $m \leq n$. Prove the sequence is either bounded or linear (i.e., $a_n = na_1$ for all $n$).
